Checked handshake errors, relay vs direct paths and DNS after the restart

The restart fixed most of it, but there is still about a second of delay on every request.

Before and after (same page)
	Earlier	Your capture at 20:38
Blocked	31 s	0
TLS handshake	25.3 s	2.4 s
Waiting for first reply	11.8 s	0.85 s
Page fully loaded	1 min 9 s	8 s

This capture was taken before I changed the DNS, so the improvement comes from the Tailscale restart alone. There have been no failed handshakes or failed dials in the 5 minutes since the restart, and the server is now using 1.1.1.1.

What is still slow

    Every request to the site waits 0.7 to 2 s before its first byte. Even the tiny /api/auth/status call waited 0.9 s. The server answers it in about 10 ms, so the delay is in transit.
    Google Fonts in the same capture took 88 ms. Your own internet is fine, so the delay is on the Tailscale path to this machine.
    All 23 of Tailscale’s public entry servers still reach this machine through relays. None has a direct path, because the router’s strict NAT doesn’t let them in directly. That is where the roughly 1 s per request comes from.

The lasting fix is on the router

    Forward UDP port 41641 on the router to this machine, 192.168.1.157. UPnP isn’t available, so this has to be set by hand.
    Tailscale can then accept direct connections. I can verify afterwards that the entry servers show as direct and the delay drops.
    It takes a few minutes in the router’s admin page, under Port Forwarding, Virtual Server or NAT. If your ISP gives you a shared address, it won’t work, and the earlier WAN-IP check on the router’s status page would show that.

Two other things in the capture

    /api/auth/status returned authenticated: false. The pipeline site doesn’t see you as signed in, and the log shows a sign-in attempt at the end returning 401 (wrong username or password). You’ll need to sign in again.
    The saved file contains your session cookie. This one is already invalid, but strip cookies before sharing a capture like this.

Once you’ve made the router change, or if you want to test the DNS change first, capture the page again and I’ll compare
